notes.title: New game from the creator of Visibility -- Hexvade!
notes.content:
Hello! 

So it's been a while (over a year, in fact) since Visbility became free to play and I promised everybody that paid money for the game a discount on the next game I create. Do not fear, I've not forgotten!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8802158/4cb5655cde27ca54b6639670fefc02665ae01c83.png[/img]

There is a totally free to play demo of the new game - Hexvade - along with a trailer at http://www.hexvade.com - feel free to go and check it out! The demo version is limited local multiplayer only and has limited characters, but rest assured the full version will have singleplayer and online multiplayer modes, this demo is just a taster! Hexvade is far more stable, bug-free and polished than Visibility is (not that that was hard, I look back on this game and cringe  a little :p)

The full game is planned for release sometime in early 2018, but that's subject to change as things in life come and go giving me either more or less time to work on Hexvade. 

I won't be posting many more announcements on here (one more when the game releases, and that'll be it most likely) so if you like the look of Hexvade and are interested in following along with the development, hit us up on social media!

Twitter: http://www.twitter.com/Hexvade
Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/Hexvade
Discord: http://discord.gg/b6FvGjb

Thank you all for reading, and I hope the new game is to your liking!

- Zeritum

notes.title: Behind the Scenes
notes.content:
Hey all! Just thought I'd give you a sneak peek into the updates which will be coming your way at some point in the future for the 1.1 update! Don't expect anything too soon but be assured that I am indeed working on it.

Please note that all of these features are still only ideas and it is not 100% certain that they'll make it into the final release.

First up, the smaller features that don't really need much explanation:

 - More levels with more mechanics
 - Level Select screen
 - Controller support
 - More achievements

Now onto a couple of the big things I have planned.

EASY MODE:
Some people have complained about the difficulty of the game. Whilst the game was intended to be a challenging game, I understand this may not be in everyone's best interests. I am planning an easy mode which means that your lights will illuminate a little bit more than they do currently. In addition, you also get an extra light on every level.

However, I don't want this to affect the player who choose to play on Normal Mode, so I will have a separate set of achievements for Easy Mode. If you complete an achievement in Normal Mode, it'll give you the achievement in both Easy and Normal modes so you don't have to go back and complete the whole game again.

MULTIPLE SAVE FILES:
People who share computers may be happy to see this. Multiple saves! You'll be able to select and save your individual save file. In theory, if I do it correctly, there will be no limit to the amount of save files you can have! You just need to name each one upon creation and then the rest works from there as it always has done.

As I said at the start, there will probably be features from this that aren't included, and there'll be some features included that aren't written here! It's just the way things go. If you have any suggestions then please do leave them as a comment, I'll read every single one of them, I swear!

Apologies for the long post but if you made it this far then good on you! :p

Hope you're all having fun and frustration with the game

-Z

notes.title: An important update regarding saves
notes.content:
Visibility has been updated, which is good! Also, bad.

This update has unfortunately broken your current save games! :( I am very sorry for the inconvenience caused but there was simply no way around it. The reason for this is that I have changed the structure of the saves to future proof them, as currently they would break if the game ever got the point where it had over 100 levels. Better to do it now rather than later!

But good news, too! This game adds a fullscreen mode, as requested by a few of you. This should fully function for all 16:9 resolutions, but it is untested on 4:3 so please be aware that it may look incredibly weird on these monitors.

That is all, and once again I am sorry for the save corruptions!

-Z
